topic: Why the CCB changes in July: the benefit year runs July–June and payments are recalculated every July from the previous year's adjusted family net income (July 2026–June 2027 uses 2025 returns); amounts are indexed to inflation each July (child under 6: $7,997 → $8,157; 6–17: $6,748 → $6,883); reduction starts above $38,237 AFNI

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Priya's family AFNI rose from $60,000 (2024) to $70,000 (2025); the July 2026–June 2027 CCB is computed on the $70,000 (above the $38,237 reduction threshold, so the income part of the calculation reduces the benefit more). Exact CCB amount not computed in the video.

spoken.old_max: seven thousand nine hundred and ninety-seven
spoken.new_max: eight thousand one hundred and fifty-seven dollars

sources.july: canada.ca CRA 'How much you can get – CCB': payments recalculated every July using the prior year's adjusted family net income; July 2026–June 2027 based on the 2025 tax year; CCB indexed to inflation; reduction thresholds $38,237 and $82,847 (via canada.ca search excerpts 2026-11-05)
sources.amounts: canada.ca CRA: July 2026–June 2027 up to $8,157 ($679.75/mo) under 6, $6,883 ($573.58/mo) 6–17; July 2025–June 2026: $7,997 under 6, $6,748 6–17 (ESDC July 2025 release)
sources.period: CRA T4114 Canada Child Benefit: the payment period runs from July 1 of the year after the base year to June 30 of the next year
